chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Conn bass sax and rubber mouthpieces
summary: He liked the Conn bass sax, rarely used baritone, and used rubber mouthpieces before the Link caught on.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: The bass -- the Conn I liked. But I would've got a bass saxophone, but the Conn was -- The bass was -- they made a real good bass saxophone. And it had a tremendous sound to it.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

The quality to it was good. And a lot of people just recently -- a lot of the guys changed their bass saxophone (inaudible) because it had that low E-flat on it (inaudible). But I never did bother -- I didn't bother about changing to bass anymore, because I wasn't using it that much.
I didn't use the baritone. I just used the baritone when we didn't have a baritone player (inaudible).
Like when the time I came I had an alto and I had played with Hamp and I had left, he asked me to come in to play (inaudible). He say, "Come on and play some third alto. I need a third alto player."
I just had left him (inaudible) playing Lucky Thomas and Arnie Cobb was still in the band. They was still in the band.
I had a rubber mouthpiece, and everybody was using that rubber mouthpiece at that
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Berg Larson hadn't come along at that time.
No. Berg Larson hadn't came out. It was one before his.
Yeah, I think it was Brilhart. That was a good one too. We had a couple of rubber mouthpieces we were using. We wasn't using the Link. But all of sudden we put on a drive for the Link.
